title: Hankel determinant bound for functions in the class U with vanishing second coefficient
statement:
Let $f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_nz^n$ belong to the class $\mathcal U$, and suppose that $a_2=0$. For an integer $n\ge3$, define the second Hankel determinant by

$$
H_2(n)(f)=a_na_{n+2}-a_{n+1}^2.
$$

**Hankel determinant conjecture.** For every integer $n\ge3$,

$$
|H_2(n)(f)|=|a_na_{n+2}-a_{n+1}^2|\le1.
$$

The estimate is sharp for $f(z)=\frac{z}{1-z^2}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}z^{2n-1}$. The result extends the sharp bounds established in the paper for the cases $n=2$ and $n=4$ to all higher second Hankel determinants for functions in $\mathcal U$ with missing second coefficient; the general case remains open.
references:
**6 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2107.00442](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.00442), [arXiv:2004.04577](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04577), [arXiv:1910.00875](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.00875), [arXiv:1107.5490](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.5490), [arXiv:math/0701483](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701483).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.06771

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).
